module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil
public import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.HardyLittlewood

/-!
# Erdős Problem 855

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/855](https://www.erdosproblems.com/855)

This is an "eventually" formulation of the Second Hardy–Littlewood conjecture.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter
open scoped Nat.Prime

namespace Erdos855

/--
Erdős Problem 855 (Segal's conjecture): $\pi(x + y) \le \pi(x) + \pi(y)$
for all sufficiently large $x, y$, i.e. for all $x, y \ge N$ for some $N$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_855 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ᶠ (xy : ℕ × ℕ) in atTop ×ˢ atTop, π (xy.1 + xy.2) ≤ π xy.1 + π xy.2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos855

findings.description: The theorem docstring calls the problem "Segal's conjecture". The cited source, Erdős's own papers and the standard references never use that name. They call it the second Hardy–Littlewood conjecture, or Erdős's old conjecture "probably stated already by Hardy and Littlewood". The name also contradicts the file's own module docstring ("an 'eventually' formulation of the Second Hardy–Littlewood conjecture"). S. L. Segal wrote a 1962 paper about this inequality, but the conjecture is not his. The Lean statement itself is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/855: "Commonly known as the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture. In [Er85c] Erdős describes it as 'an old conjecture of mine which was probably already stated by Hardy and Littlewood'." [Er85c] = Erdős, 'On some of my problems in number theory I would most like to see solved', Ootacamund 1984 (users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1985-17.pdf): "An old conjecture of mine which was probably stated already by Hardy and Littlewood states π(x+y) ≤ π(x)+π(y)". [Er61] (1961-22.pdf): "It has been conjectured that π(x+y) ≤ π(x)+π(y)". Wikipedia (Second Hardy–Littlewood conjecture), MathWorld (Hardy-Littlewood Conjectures) and OEIS A023193 never mention Segal.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace "(Segal's conjecture)" with "(second Hardy–Littlewood conjecture, eventual form)" and ideally phrase it as the source's question: "Is it true that $\pi(x + y) \le \pi(x) + \pi(y)$ for all sufficiently large $x, y$, i.e. for all $x, y \ge N$ for some $N$?"

reformulations.difference: The source says "for large x and y". The Lean writes this as `∀ᶠ (xy : ℕ × ℕ) in atTop ×ˢ atTop, π (xy.1 + xy.2) ≤ π xy.1 + π xy.2` (the product filter), with x, y natural numbers, and `answer(sorry)` in `Prop` elaborating to `True`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Rewriting with `Filter.prod_atTop_atTop_eq` and then `Filter.eventually_atTop_prod_self` turns the right-hand side into `∃ N, ∀ x y, N ≤ x → N ≤ y → π (x + y) ≤ π x + π y`, i.e. "for all sufficiently large x and y". Separate thresholds for x and y give the same statement, via `Filter.eventually_prod_iff`. Since `answer(sorry)` is `True` here, the whole theorem is equivalent to that statement (`simp only [true_iff]`). Using ℕ matches Erdős's usage: [Er85c] says "Call an integer x 'good' if for all integers y < x…", and the second Hardy–Littlewood conjecture is standardly stated for integers x, y ≥ 2.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/855 (via https://r.jina.ai/ proxy; rendered HTML with MathJax data-latex extracted)
review.notes:
The single theorem states the problem the source poses. I found no misformalization; the only finding is a minor docstring naming slip.

Checks behind this:
(1) Eventual reading. erdosproblems.com asks the question \"for large x and y\" and tags it \"cannot be resolved with a finite computation\". A forum comment (Dogmachine, 12 Jan 2026) says the problem is about \"the regime of large x and y\" and that no single counterexample suffices. Readings where only one variable, or only x+y, is large would be trivially false: with y = 1, π(x+1) > π(x) + π(1) whenever x+1 is prime, which I checked numerically. So ∃N ∀x,y ≥ N is the right reading. The Hensley–Richards conditional disproof (for every large y, infinitely many x) works in this regime.
(2) Domain. A real-variable reading would be formally stronger: it amounts to π(a+b+1) ≤ π(a)+π(b) for large integers a, b. Erdős's texts, however, use integers ([Er85c]: \"Call an integer x 'good' if for all integers y < x …\"; [Er61]: \"verified it for y ≤ 41\"). The classical conjecture is stated for integers x, y ≥ 2 (Wikipedia, MathWorld, Richards), and the real version for all x, y ≥ 2 is trivially false (x = y = 2.5). So ℕ is the faithful choice.
(3) Lean checks. `answer(sorry)` in `Prop` elaborates to `True` by default, so the theorem is the positive claim, matching the source's \"is it true that…\". `π` is `Nat.primeCounting` (primes ≤ n); it agrees with a sieve on small inputs, and there are no violations for 2 ≤ x, y ≤ 400. Nothing in the statement is trivially provable or refutable (no truncated subtraction, division or empty types).
(4) Status. OPEN on erdosproblems.com (page edited 08 Apr 2026) and in teorth/erdosproblems; the file says `research open`, so there is no status issue.
(5) The page's variants (Straus's π(x)+2π(y/2); Erdős's O(y/(log y)^2) weakening; Erdős–Richards density of good x; the [Er80] conjecture) are not formalized. Omitting them is not a defect.

I could not open Segal's 1962 Trans. AMS paper (blocked). The naming finding rests on the cited source, Erdős's papers, Wikipedia, MathWorld and OEIS, none of which call this Segal's conjecture.
